blocks.value: This is a short lesson, and it is mostly a name for something you have already been doing. But it introduces one idea worth having explicitly: **every expression has a type, and that type is decided before the result is stored.**
That single fact explains the integer-division bug from Lesson 3, and most of the surprises still ahead of you.
What you will be able to do
By the end of this lesson you will be able to:

items: Define an expression and identify one in code
Apply the two rules for evaluating mixed expressions
Trace a logical expression to its boolean result
